name: Signal Independence & Actionability Audit
purpose: Identify near-redundant signals using within-date rank correlation.
Separate FAVOR evidence from AVOID evidence.
Produce the nonredundant candidate set that R3 is permitted to consider.
principles: R2.1 does not fit a combined model.
R2.1 does not change or rerun R2 evidence thresholds.
Redundancy is measured within each monthly ETF cross-section, not by pooled correlation across dates.
A feature is not called FAVOR-actionable merely because it ranks ETFs; its favorable side must itself beat SPY with statistically positive evidence.
A feature may still be useful as AVOID evidence when its unfavorable side persistently lags SPY.
All actionability thresholds are frozen in this spec before R2.1 is run.

bootstrap.method: moving block bootstrap over monthly extreme-group metrics

favor_requires: 95% block-bootstrap CI for favorable-side mean SPY-relative return entirely above 0
95% block-bootstrap CI for favorable-side SPY-beating rate entirely above 0.50
avoid_requires: 95% block-bootstrap CI for unfavorable-side mean SPY-relative return entirely below 0
95% block-bootstrap CI for unfavorable-side SPY-beating rate entirely below 0.50
separation_requires: 95% block-bootstrap CI for oriented FAVOR-minus-AVOID relative-return spread entirely above 0

representative_preference: Prefer original economically interpretable features over cross-sectional percentile transforms.
Prefer absolute-return momentum over same-date SPY-relative momentum when their rankings are exactly equivalent.
Prefer features with broader month-end coverage.
Use stronger R2 evidence only after the interpretability/coverage rules above.
